newsitem.title: USA: Skaters are next in-line for L.A. Marathon.
newsitem.headline: Skaters are next in-line for L.A. Marathon.

text.p: For the first time, next month's Los Angeles Marathon will feature the bane of many runners' lives: in-line skaters.
"One day I stopped and thought, 'why not?'" the race's president William Burke told the Los Angeles Times Monday.
Burke said he had been badgered into opening the Marathon to in-line skaters by his barber, who is an avid skater.
However, the 30,000 runners, cyclists and wheel-chair participants in the March 2 race will not have to worry about avoiding skaters weaving in and out of the route.
The skaters will start after the others and will compete in a 10-km "fun skate" on a separate course. There will also be a separate race for professional skaters, Burke said.

Although in-line skaters are as common as surfers in the beach towns of southern California, the idea of them taking part in races with runners was not so well received in Boston and New York - homes of America's two traditional Marathons.

"It won't ever happen in this town," said Lesley Kurz, a spokesman for the 100-year-old Boston Marathon. "We have a rich tradition to uphold here, so I don't think any in-line skaters are going to compete here any time soon.
"And that's the way out runners like it," he told the Times.
New York Marathon director Allan Steinfield didn't think the idea was right for his city either. "New York is just too congested," he told the newspaper.
